summary: Returns a dictionary mapping every permutation of two lowercase English letters to its occurrence count as an adjacent bigram in the input word, defaulting to 0 for unobserved pairs.
input_domain: Strings consisting exclusively of lowercase English alphabetic characters (a-z), with length greater than or equal to 0.

items.behavior: Distinct adjacent bigrams are counted correctly
items.expected: Dictionary contains 650 keys; 'ab': 1, 'bc': 1, 'cd': 1, all other keys 0
items.rationale: Spec states: 'The dictionary values represent the frequency of these two-letter combinations in the given word.'
Spec defines values as frequency counts; standard n-gram frequency counting processes overlapping adjacent pairs sequentially.

items.behavior: Empty input yields all zero counts
items.rationale: Spec guarantees: 'If a combination does not appear in the word, its value will be 0.' An empty string contains no combinations.

items.behavior: Single character input yields all zero counts
items.rationale: No two-letter combinations can be formed from a single character, triggering the zero-value rule for all keys.

items.behavior: Keys exactly match permutations of 2 lowercase letters
items.rationale: Spec requires: 'The function uses the itertools.permutations method to generate all two-letter combinations of alphabets.'

items.expected: All values in result are instances of int and >= 0
items.rationale: Values represent frequencies/counts, which are mathematically constrained to non-negative integers.
Spec defines values as frequency counts in the given word; multiple occurrences accumulate.

items.behavior: Keys with identical letters are absent due to permutations constraint
items.expected: Key ('a','a') is absent from dictionary; all present keys have value 0
items.rationale: Spec mandates itertools.permutations, which yields ordered selections without replacement from unique source characters, excluding identical-pair keys.

ambiguities: Handling of non-alphabetic characters (e.g., digits, punctuation, whitespace) in the input string is not specified.
Case sensitivity: whether uppercase input should be normalized to lowercase before counting is not stated.
Exact counting mechanism for overlapping substrings (e.g., whether 'aaa' counts 'aa' once or twice) is not explicitly defined.
Behavior when passed non-string types (e.g., None, int) is undefined; spec does not declare a precondition or explicit exception type.
